models.text: The suite should implement force and moment equilibrium, rigid-body sliding equilibrium, overturning moment equilibrium, bearing-pressure distribution, Cauchy stress equilibrium, Hooke's law, Euler–Bernoulli and Timoshenko beam formulations, plate bending theories, shell theory, Euler buckling, plate buckling, von Mises yielding and nonlinear finite-element structural models.

models.group: Seabed bearing capacity and settlement models
models.text: The suite should include Terzaghi bearing-capacity theory, Meyerhof bearing-capacity formulations, Hansen and Vesic bearing-capacity methods, Skempton undrained bearing-capacity approaches, shallow-foundation capacity models, combined vertical–horizontal–moment loading envelopes, effective-area methods, elastic settlement theory, one-dimensional Terzaghi consolidation, Biot poroelasticity, nonlinear stress-dependent soil stiffness, Modified Cam-Clay, critical-state soil mechanics, Mohr–Coulomb plasticity and Drucker–Prager plasticity.

These calculations should employ Coulomb friction theory, interface adhesion models, undrained shear strength-based sliding resistance, drained frictional resistance, passive soil resistance formulations, seabed penetration models, large-deformation soil mechanics, nonlinear contact formulations, uplift resistance models, suction breakout models and cyclic soil degradation models.

The suite should include Morison wave-current loading, near-bed velocity profile models, Keulegan–Carpenter parameter relationships, Reynolds-number-dependent drag, sediment critical mobility through Shields-type formulations, bed shear stress models, local scour prediction methods and sediment transport models appropriate to the seabed material.

The suite should include submerged-weight and buoyancy calculations, Archimedes' principle, lowering line dynamics, rigid-body hydrodynamic motion, added-mass models, seabed touchdown contact, nonlinear impact mechanics, energy-based dropped-object methods, local elastic–plastic impact analysis, S–N fatigue assessment and Miner cumulative damage.

The suite should combine detailed structural finite-element analysis with nonlinear geotechnical finite elements, coupled effective stress–pore pressure analysis, large-deformation finite-element methods, coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian soil analysis, particle-based methods for large penetration, CFD-derived environmental loads, structural contact mechanics and probabilistic soil-property analysis. These coupled approaches are particularly relevant when assessing mudmat embedment, skirt penetration, soil failure mechanisms and installation-stage response.

subtitle: On-bottom stability, seabed bearing, sliding, overturning, settlement, lifting, lowering and seabed interaction.
ic: The initial conditions shall establish the three-dimensional geometry of the mudmat, subsea template, manifold support, protective frame or other subsea support structure. The geometry shall include structural members, plates, skirts, braces, equipment supports, lifting points and the location of the overall centre of gravity.

The initial seabed conditions shall specify bathymetry, seabed slope, soil stratigraphy, undisturbed or remoulded shear strength, effective stresses, pore-water pressure, stiffness, compressibility and the initial sediment surface. The initial contact state shall identify whether the structure rests directly on the seabed, is partially embedded or is supported by skirts or foundation elements.

For on-bottom analysis, the structure shall be initialized in its installed equilibrium condition under submerged self-weight, equipment weight and any sustained pipeline or jumper reactions. The starting condition shall include the corresponding seabed contact pressures, settlements and rotations where these have already developed.

For lowering and landing analysis, the initial conditions shall specify the suspended structure position, orientation, lowering velocity, rigging tensions and separation from the seabed. Settlement simulations shall start from the selected installation or post-installation consolidation state. Fatigue and damage analyses shall incorporate initial corrosion, existing cracks and accumulated cyclic damage where applicable.
bc: Seabed boundaries shall provide vertical bearing resistance, horizontal friction, possible uplift separation, passive soil resistance and nonlinear soil deformation. Contact shall permit separation, sliding and local penetration where these behaviours are physically relevant.

Hydrodynamic boundaries shall apply wave-induced and current-induced forces at the submerged surfaces of the structure and associated equipment. The water level, seawater density, near-bed current velocity and hydrodynamic load direction shall be defined.

Structural boundaries shall include equipment support loads, manifold operating loads, pipeline end reactions, jumper connection forces and thermal expansion loads. These reactions may vary with operating pressure, temperature, connected pipeline displacement and equipment operating condition.

For suction and penetration analysis, skirt boundaries shall include soil resistance, external hydrostatic pressure and appropriate internal suction pressure. For landing analysis, the lifting line shall apply tension and prescribed lowering motion while seabed contact develops progressively. Accidental loading boundaries shall define dropped-object impact conditions, contact stiffness and impact locations.

For settlement and consolidation, drainage boundaries shall distinguish drained, undrained and partially drained conditions as appropriate to the soil model. Scour modelling shall apply the relevant seabed flow, sediment transport and evolving seabed elevation conditions.

calibration: Calibration should use site-specific seabed investigations, cone penetration tests, laboratory shear tests, consolidation tests, interface shear tests, plate load tests and instrumented foundation experiments. Mudmat–soil friction coefficients, soil adhesion, undrained shear strength, stiffness, bearing resistance and settlement parameters should be calibrated against measured behaviour under representative vertical, horizontal and moment loading.

For on-bottom stability analysis, hydrodynamic drag and inertia coefficients should be calibrated using laboratory flume measurements, wave-current basin tests and field observations of comparable subsea structures. The influence of structural shape, seabed proximity, shielding and current direction should be considered.

Sliding and overturning resistance models should use measured interface friction, passive soil resistance, foundation embedment and load eccentricity. Settlement and differential settlement models should be calibrated against laboratory consolidation tests, physical foundation tests and measured seabed installations.
Suction penetration, skirt installation and uplift breakout models should be calibrated using instrumented penetration and pullout experiments, supported by representative field installation records.
Pipeline and jumper interface stiffness and reaction loading should be calibrated using measured connector loads, pipeline displacement records and laboratory connector tests when available.
Dropped-object impact and local structural response models should be informed by material coupon testing and representative impact experiments.
verification: Verification should include analytical checks for submerged weight, buoyancy, hydrostatic pressure, vertical equilibrium, sliding resistance, overturning moments and foundation bearing pressure.

Structural finite-element formulations should be checked against established plate, shell, beam and frame benchmarks. Mesh convergence should focus on mudmat plate bending, skirt intersections, equipment supports, weld details and localized contact stresses.

Soil contact formulations should undergo contact-pressure convergence studies, friction implementation tests, uplift separation checks and soil plasticity benchmarks. Numerical results should be insensitive to reasonable mesh and solver tolerance refinement.
Bearing capacity, sliding, overturning, embedment and settlement calculations should be checked using independent geotechnical benchmark solutions and published reference cases.
Hydrodynamic force calculations should be verified under idealized current and wave loading before applying irregular sea states.
Lowering and landing simulations should undergo time-step convergence, dynamic equilibrium checks and contact-impact verification.
Suction installation models should be tested for consistent pressure loading, penetration resistance, drainage assumptions and changing contact conditions.
validation: On-bottom stability predictions should be compared against independent wave-current flume experiments and recorded field behaviour of mudmats, templates and subsea equipment.

Bearing capacity and settlement predictions should be validated using representative laboratory foundation tests, centrifuge tests, instrumented field installations and subsequent settlement measurements.
Mudmat sliding and overturning predictions should be assessed using combined-loading experiments that reproduce expected vertical, horizontal and moment actions.
Suction and uplift resistance predictions should be compared with measured penetration and breakout data.
Structural stresses and deformations should be compared against instrumented laboratory tests of representative frames, plates, supports and subsea structural assemblies.
Landing response predictions should be assessed using recorded lowering tensions, touchdown accelerations and seabed contact behaviour.
Scour and long-term foundation response should be compared with repeat subsea surveys, remotely operated vehicle observations and independent geotechnical measurements.

Validation should distinguish short-term installation behaviour from long-term operational behaviour, particularly where cyclic loading, soil consolidation and seabed erosion alter support conditions.

geometry.text: Mudmat foundations, subsea templates, manifold supports, protection structures, guideposts, suction foundations, foundation skirts and supported subsea equipment.

geometry.cat: Conventional and universal CAD geometry formats
geometry.text: STEP, IGES, Parasolid, ACIS, IFC, DXF and supported DWG should be accepted for mudmat plates, structural beams, skirts, subsea support frames, gussets, lifting points, equipment supports and pipeline interface geometries.

IFC where appropriate, structural member models in SDNF or structured JSON/XML, subsea installation layouts in CSV/XYZ, foundation footprint polygons and digital seabed surface geometry should be supported. Pipe connection interfaces and equipment orientation should be preserved so that imported structures can receive realistic operational reaction loads.
Abaqus INP, Nastran BDF, ANSYS CDB, Gmsh MSH, MED, UNV, VTK/VTU and Exodus should be accepted for plates, shells, structural solids, seabed contact interfaces and continuum foundation models.

STL, OBJ, PLY, GLB, LAS/LAZ, E57, GeoTIFF, ESRI ASCII Grid, XYZ bathymetry, LandXML and point-cloud-derived seabed meshes should be supported. These are particularly useful for importing realistic seabed irregularities, partially embedded mudmats, surveyed support structures and as-installed subsea geometry.
